newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees to open textiles market.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees to open textiles market.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers agreed on Monday to confirm earlier undertakings to open up the bloc's textiles market by bringing additional product categories within the scope of world trade rules.
The deal confirms EU undertakings made within the Uruguay Round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) after several years of multi-country trade talks which concluded in December 1993.

"The agreement reached today represents the EU's second stage of this process and involves the integration (into international trade rules) of 23 different categories of product," the European Commission said in a statement.

Products covered included a variety of fibres, fabrics and yarns as well as women's shawls and scarves, stockings and socks, women's suits, industrial clothing, ski-suits and swimwear, the statement said.
"I am delighted that member states have been able to find broad agreement on such a potentially controversial subject," European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said in the statement.
"It demonstrates that the EU is prepared and willing to go beyond its legal requirements under the World Trade Organisation textiles agreement," he added.
The WTO took over from the GATT on January 1, 1995 as the world's main trade watchdog body.

The original GATT deal included an undertaking to wind down over 10 years the existing Multi-Fibre Arrangement - a system of restrictive import quotas imposed by rich nations on textile goods and apparel from poorer nations.
Figures from 1994 put the value of the world textiles trade at more than $200 billion.
